Transposition of Great Arteries

qs.q: In Transposition of Great Arteries (TGA), which embryological failure is responsible?
o: Failure of the aorticopulmonary septum to spiral
Atrophy of the right aortic arch
qs.e: TGA occurs when the aorticopulmonary septum fails to spiral normally, resulting in the aorta arising from the RV and the pulmonary artery from the LV.
qs.s: Weekly Pathology Exam - March 7, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: In Transposition of Great Arteries, which embryological failure is directly responsible?
o: Resorption of subpulmonary instead of subaortic conus
Failure of subaortic conus to elongate
Failure of truncus arteriosus to partition
Malalignment of the outlet septum anteriorly
qs.e: Normally the subaortic conus resorbs, moving the aorta posteriorly to connect with the LV. In TGA the wrong conus resorbs, keeping the aorta anterior and connected to the RV.
